record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and a truncated file listing only; the linked paper and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README discusses refusal directions as a contrast, but reports results about pass/fail transcript evidence and coding-agent actions, not refusal behavior or the harmful-minus-harmless refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The README describes a different construct: a pass/fail transcript signal in static coding-agent prompts. It reports projection, patching, and action-choice results, but does not test refusal, harmful requests, or the refusal direction in any listed claim version. The results below are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study (README only) measures a residual direction for pass/fail test-transcript evidence in coding-agent prompts and its effect on an edit-vs-noop logit margin. It never measures refusal, harmful requests, or the harmful-minus-harmless direction. It mentions refusal directions only once, as a contrast. So it neither tests nor uses the claim. 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses' because there is a single contrastive sentence and no argument about any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The record should add three points from the README. Rank-1 steering reproduces the shift. A regex or bag-of-words baseline matches or beats the projection on the transcript formats tested. An internal-state edit-veto is no better than reading the transcript. The authors explicitly contrast their direction with a refusal direction that controls behaviour.
record.recipe_differences: Research paper, code, and analysis-artifact repository; not a refusal-direction replication. Its README describes transcript-evidence projections and patching in coding-agent prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports that the projection follows the transcript rather than code correctness when those conflict, and is near chance without a transcript on Qwen. It says full causal localization is Qwen-only; the other models have reported-cell submargin effects.

fits_no_version.finding: A single residual direction encoding transcript pass/fail separates prompts: ROC-AUC 0.989/0.950/0.888 (Qwen/CodeGemma/DeepSeek). A regex or bag-of-words baseline matches or beats it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-transcript pass/fail evidence is linearly available in small code models' residual streams at the action position.

fits_no_version.finding: Patching or rank-1 steering along the layer-24 Qwen direction moves the edit-minus-noop margin, but the chosen action never changes. Noop is selected in 0% of prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlike a refusal direction that controls behaviour, this evidence direction shifts a decision submargin without flipping the action, because of a strong first-token action prior.

fits_no_version.finding: The projection follows the transcript rather than code correctness, and is near chance on Qwen when no transcript is shown.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The direction tracks transcript evidence, not code correctness.

record.problems: Only the repository README and file listing are available here; the paper and code were not read or run. The README provides no uncertainty values for the reported metrics or patching effects and does not state prompt counts for the action-choice percentages.
record.rows_left_out: No README-reported related results were omitted.

untested.parts: No refusal direction, ablation, addition or capability check; the direction studied encodes transcript pass/fail evidence.
No weight edit or refusal evaluation.
No transfer of a refusal direction.

record.verdict_notes: Only the README is available; this is a non-peer-reviewed preprint repo. The mention of refusal directions is a one-line contrast and gives no evidence on any version. The record omits the steering and text-baseline results, but these concern the study's own construct, not the claim, so they are not 'missing' for versions.

No refusal-direction weight edit or refusal evaluation.
No test of attacks suppressing the refusal direction or training against its ablation.
No comparison of refusal directions, cones, affine structures, or additional refusal components.
No measurement of harmfulness judgment or refusal decisions.
No refusal-direction transfer test across languages, model variants, or training stages.
No test of how refusal training affects the direction.
